sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Area Operators
sections.content: Briefly recall that a 2x2 determinant represents the signed area of a parallelogram formed by two column vectors. If the determinant is zero, the vectors are collinear (area collapses).
sections.example: Visualizing two vectors, v1=(2,1) and v2=(1,2), forming a parallelogram in the Cartesian plane.

sections.title: The Linear System as a Geometric Puzzle
sections.content: Represent the system Ax = b as a vector equation: x1(column1) + x2(column2) = b. Explain that we are trying to find the 'weights' (x1, x2) that scale these columns to reach target vector b.
sections.example: An archer (the vector b) stands at (5, 5). Two elastic bands (column vectors) must be stretched by factors x1 and x2 to hit the bullseye.

sections.title: Geometric Substitution (Cramer's Insight)
sections.content: Introduce Cramer’s Rule: x1 = det(A1)/det(A) and x2 = det(A2)/det(A). Explain that substituting the target vector b into the first column creates a new parallelogram whose area is scaled by x1.
sections.example: Animation showing the original parallelogram defined by (col1, col2) being swapped for (b, col2) to reveal the area ratio.

sections.title: Visual Proof: Area Scaling
sections.content: Demonstrate that the ratio of the area of the 'substituted' parallelogram to the original parallelogram is exactly the value of the unknown variable. This provides the 'Aha!' moment.
sections.example: A split-screen animation: Left side shows the variable x1 changing; right side shows the area of the modified parallelogram expanding and contracting in perfect synchronization.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Constraint
sections.content: Conclude by noting that if det(A)=0, the column vectors are parallel (the area is zero), making division impossible—this is the geometric reason why systems with no unique solutions fail Cramer's Rule.
sections.example: The 'Crushed Parallelogram': Two column vectors collapsing into a single line, rendering the target vector b unreachable unless it lies on that same line.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Area Operators
lecture_lines: Determinants represent the area of a parallelogram.
Zero determinant means area collapses to zero.
animations: Show a 2D plane with two vectors labeled v1 and v2 in #FF00FF and #00FFFF.
Highlight the area spanned by v1 and v2 in #FFFFFF with 20% opacity.

storyboard.title: The Linear System as a Geometric Puzzle
lecture_lines: Systems of equations form a geometric puzzle.
Represent Ax equals b as a vector combination.
We solve for weights reaching the target vector.
animations: Draw a 2D coordinate system #FFFFFF, plot vectors.
Animate v1 and v2 being scaled to reach b.
Flash the scalar values representing the weights.

storyboard.title: Geometric Substitution (Cramer's Insight)
lecture_lines: Cramer's Rule relates areas to variables.
Swap columns with the target vector.
Substituted areas scale with the unknown weight.
Ratio of these areas yields the variable.
This reveals the geometry behind the rule.
animations: Show initial parallelogram formed by v1 and v2.
Replace one column with target vector b.
Calculate area ratio of the new parallelogram.
Show the weight value emerging from ratio.

storyboard.title: Visual Proof: Area Scaling
lecture_lines: Area scaling proves the variable's value.
Watch the parallelogram expand and contract.
The area ratio equals the unknown weight.
This confirms Cramer's algebraic result visually.
animations: Show the two parallelograms side by side in #FFFFFF.
Animate the scaling factor applied to v1.
Overlay the area value calculation on the screen.
Sync the area growth with the variable weight value.
Fade out showing final proof equivalence.

storyboard.title: Summary and Geometric Constraint
lecture_lines: Singular systems have a zero determinant.
Columns collapse into a single line.
animations: Shrink the parallelogram until area becomes zero.
Show the target vector 'b' outside the span.
